speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
text: asked the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (a) what are the top 10 SkillsFuture courses that Singaporeans have signed up for; (b) what is the percentage of utilisation of SkillsFuture funds for these top 10 courses; (c) what is the profile of the SkillsFuture users who have utilised the funds for these top 10 courses; and (d) which of these courses lead to new or better jobs.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Members might have noticed some titles are the same because they are delivered by different training providers.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: A more meaningful way to look at it is to cluster popular courses into certain sectors and look at the entire cluster.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: If we look from that perspective, the most popular area of training is still Information and Communications Technology (ICT)-related courses.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Notwithstanding, one of the key objectives of the SkillsFuture Credit scheme in supporting the SkillsFuture Movement is to empower individuals to take ownership of their skills development, open up their minds to embrace a lifelong learning mindset and embark on the journey.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Judging by the take-up and the types of courses most people enrolled in, we believe the scheme has achieved this objective.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Some courses, such as cooking classes, Korean language classes, are hailed as SkillsFuture classes.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: What is the approach that we take in order to determine whether any particular course can tap on the SkillsFuture funding?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I have explained this point quite a few times in Parliament but I think it needs to be further repeated.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: One, SkillsFuture Credit is one feature of a much larger scheme, programme and movement called SkillsFuture.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: For those courses that we spent $700 million on, we curate them carefully.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We enrol trainees based on whether they are really pursuing that career, and they will be guided and the results measured.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: SkillsFuture Credit, on the other hand, is really to open up the minds of everyone that you have a $500 voucher, so start thinking about how to upgrade and, really, start changing the mindset to one where we all have to be responsible for our own upgrading journey.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But we do notice that the most popular courses are still the ICT courses, particularly amongst the older Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: As to whether some people pick up flower arrangement or cooking, we do not judge.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: If we put a $500 voucher in everybody's hand, we trust that people exercise their decision well to take up courses most beneficial to them.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: After all, what is leisure to me may be a profession to you.
